A purchasing decision you can audit at a glance.

ProcurePilot reads supplier quotes so a buyer doesn’t have to retype them, and an owner can approve with the evidence in view. The system is built for that: calm, dense, bilingual, and specific about every number it shows.

verifiedBrand alignment: colours and type follow docs/brand (Converge, adopted 2026-10-14). Navy is structure and action, teal is the best quote and the money saved, Readex Pro sets both languages. One documented exception: table and money figures use Noto Kufi Arabic, because Readex Pro has no tabular figures.

The reference: the medicine carton. Every Egyptian pharmacy shelf holds the same quiet discipline: a white board, one colour band, the name in Arabic and English side by side, the strength stated precisely, and a printed lot code that says where it came from.

ProcurePilot borrows exactly that. Prices are declared like a dose: amount, currency, and per what. Each extracted number carries a lot stamp back to its source page. The band is teal, the colour of the logo’s winning bar, and it means only money saved and the best offer.

  • description
    Evidence before assertionAny number pulled from a document links to its page and shows how sure the extraction is.
  • receipt_long
    Declare, never implyMoney always shows currency and unit: per pack, landed, or per kg. A bare figure is a bug.
  • verified
    A person authorisesRaised elevation is kept for items waiting on a human decision. Automation prepares; it never looks like it decided.
  • savings
    One band, one meaningTeal means money saved or best offer. Status colours mean status. Nothing is coloured for decoration.
  • translate
    Two languages, one weightArabic is never the fallback. Layout mirrors through logical properties; figures stay tabular in both.

Colour

Paper grounds, brand-navy text and actions, and one teal band taken from the logo’s best-quote bar. Success is a yellower green and info a blue, so neither reads as savings. Contrast ratios are measured live from the current theme.

Primitive ramps

Raw values only. Nothing in a component reads a primitive directly; a semantic token chooses one per theme.

Primitive → semantic → component

Three layers, read left to right. Swapping a theme changes which primitive a semantic token points at; components never change.

Typography

Readex Pro is one family drawn for Arabic and Latin together, so a mixed Arabic and English row keeps one baseline and one voice. Titles use it at 600 with −2% tracking on Latin only; Arabic is never tracked. Readex Pro has no tabular figures, so numbers in tables and money columns use Noto Kufi Arabic (tabular Latin and Arabic-Indic digits); everything else stays Readex Pro.

Money formatting (live, follows language)

CaseThis page’s languageArabic, Western digits

Formatted with Intl.NumberFormat from the tenant’s currency. Negative amounts take a minus sign, never colour alone. Western digits in Arabic is a per-user preference, not a separate locale.

Motion

Motion confirms a change; it never decorates. Entrances ease out, exits are shorter and ease in. Press Play to compare.

--pp-dur-fast · 120ms--pp-ease

--pp-dur-slow · 320ms--pp-ease-in-out
Moving between two resting places: drawer, reorder
--pp-dur-fast · 120ms--pp-ease-exit
Leaving: dismissed toast, closed menu

Feedback

Say what happened, then what to do next. Alerts sit in the page where the problem is; toasts confirm something already done; a dialog interrupts only to protect a purchase.

Tokens

Our tokens are the source; Angular Material 19 reads them through its system variables. Map once in the global stylesheet, then components inherit.
